page: Amazon Web Services m8gd.metal-24xl is a bare-metal general-purpose cloud instance built on the ARMv9 architecture using 96-core AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 processors operating at 2.8 GHz. The server offers dedicated physical CPU cores with one thread per core, backed by 64 KB L1 data cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 36 MB L3 cache. It incorporates 384 GB of DDR5 memory, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The configuration includes 5,700 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage and provides a baseline network throughput of 40 Gbps, operating without hardware GPU acceleration.

Benchmark evaluation demonstrates top-tier multi-core computing capability, reflected in high stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-threaded metrics, as well as software compilation and ray tracing tests. Memory subsystems achieve robust throughput with cached read speeds exceeding 11,000 GB/sec and uncached read bandwidth reaching 481.33 GB/sec. Conversely, single-core CPU execution sits within average performance brackets across stress-ng and Geekbench. While extended precision and large language model inference deliver acceptable throughput for medium and large token processing, lightweight token generation yields lower comparative throughput.

With its high core density, substantial DDR5 capacity, and fast local NVMe storage array, this bare-metal platform provides efficient resource utilization for multi-threaded enterprise services without virtualization overhead. The combination of high database operational rates and rapid Redis throughput makes it an effective deployment target for distributed transactional databases, large caching layers, high-volume static web serving, Clang compilation pipelines, and parallel data engineering workloads.
description: Amazon Web Services m8gd.metal-24xl is a bare-metal general-purpose server powered by 96 dedicated ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 cores clocked at 2.8 GHz. The platform features 384 GB of DDR5 RAM with 4.0 GB per core, 5,700 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, and 40 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, operating without discrete GPU accelerators. Benchmarks reveal top-tier multi-threaded compute and memory performance, evidenced by high Geekbench multi-core scores, software compilation efficiency, and over 200 million Redis SET operations per second. While single-thread benchmarks remain in the middle tier, the high parallel processing throughput and fast local storage deliver balanced resource efficiency. The server is well positioned for demanding multi-threaded workloads, including distributed transactional databases, large-scale Redis in-memory caches, high-throughput static web serving, software build clusters, and parallel data processing pipelines.
